currentContext.strengths: Diversified portfolio of 18,400+ SKUs spanning personal computing, enterprise infrastructure, components, storage, networking, lifestyle and emerging technology, enabling multi-segment participation across consumer, SMB and enterprise customers.|Long-standing brand relationships: of 78 global technology brands represented, 23 brands associated for over 5 years contribute 88% of revenue, and 11 brands with relationships exceeding 10 years contribute 72% of revenue.|One of India's largest ICT distribution ecosystems — 55 branches, 71 warehouses and presence across 700+ locations, serving 10,300+ partners and B2B customers across general trade, modern trade and e-commerce.|Early mover in semiconductor distribution — first ICT distributor in India to enter the segment (2021) — supported by a dedicated Embedded Lab in Bengaluru.
currentContext.strategies: Evolve from a distribution business into a broader technology solutions partner, resting on three priorities: strengthening the core personal computing/enterprise/components engine, developing higher-margin higher-growth verticals with semiconductors at the centre, and pursuing margin expansion by integrating across the value chain into solutions and services.|For FY2027: strengthen the core, develop higher-return verticals (semiconductors, data centres, AI, software & cybersecurity, managed services) that will shape the next decade, and expand capabilities across the value chain.|Grow the semiconductor vertical further — first ICT distributor in India to enter the segment (2021), supported by a dedicated Embedded Lab in Bengaluru, with new semiconductor subsidiaries in India and Singapore strengthening dedicated operations.|Deepen presence in smaller (Tier-2/Tier-3) cities via branch network expansion, and broaden the brand portfolio through new partnerships across enterprise, education technology and premium consumer devices.|Position the Company as a partner in India's AI adoption (not only a hardware supplier) through structured AI Bootcamps and developer/enterprise engagement.|Board recommended a final dividend of Rs. 2 per equity share of Rs. 5 face value (40%) for FY2025-26, to be declared at the 37th AGM (September 9, 2026), governed by the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy under SEBI Listing Regulation 43A.
currentContext.expansion: As an asset-light ICT distributor (no manufacturing plants; BRSR discloses 0 plants and 70 domestic + 1 international office/branch locations), RP tech's 'expansion' is footprint and vertical build-out rather than physical capacity. During FY26 the Company added three new branches (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur), taking its branch network to 55 branches (71 warehouses, 700+ locations), deepening Tier-II/Tier-III presence. It strengthened its semiconductor and embedded vertical through its Bengaluru Embedded Lab (reference-design, board bring-up, PCB design and AI/ML application development) and by incorporating new semiconductor subsidiaries in India (Rashi Semiconductor Solutions Private Limited) and, after the FY26 close (post 1 April 2026), a Singapore step-down subsidiary (Rashi Semiconductor Solutions Pte Ltd, 100% held by the Indian semiconductor subsidiary) and a Dubai step-down subsidiary (Rashi Peripherals LLC-FZ, 98% held by Rashi Peripherals Pte Ltd, Singapore). It also incorporated a new wholly-owned subsidiary, RP Tech Electronics Limited. Subsequent to year-end, the Board (June 23, 2026) approved and completed (July 2, 2026) the acquisition of 67% of VDA Infosolutions Private Limited for Rs 368.50 crore cash, with the remaining 33% stake to be acquired over the next three years.
currentContext.mdna: AI PC transition (NPU-equipped devices, Copilot+ PC platform, Windows 10 end-of-support) is driving a multi-year upgrade cycle and robust demand for GPUs, AI-enabled processors, memory modules, SSDs, cooling and power-management solutions.|Enterprise refresh cycle: replacement of ageing devices and migration to AI-ready systems is accelerating commercial PC upgrades; India enterprise segment and workstation shipments grew strongly in Q1 2026.|Data-centre build-out in India (installed capacity ~1.9 GW in FY26, more than doubling from ~778 MW in FY23, with a ~4.5 GW development pipeline over the next five years) is driving demand for servers, storage, networking, power-management and cooling infrastructure.|Global and Indian semiconductor demand growth driven by AI-native infrastructure, hyperscale/cloud expansion, embedded/edge applications and supply-chain diversification is expected to increase distribution and technical-design-support opportunities.|India's IT spending is projected to reach USD176.3 billion in 2026 (+10.6% YoY), with device spending forecast to rise 9.9% to USD66.4 billion, supported by enterprise modernisation, replacement demand and AI-enabled technology adoption.|Gaming market growth (Indian gaming market projected to grow from USD4.59bn in FY25 to USD5.37bn in FY26, at a longer-term CAGR of 15.62%) driven by esports, cloud/multiplayer gaming and premiumisation of gaming devices/peripherals.

risks.note: Identified by the Risk Management Committee as a primary risk area for an ICT distributor whose SKU portfolio is exposed to rapid product-cycle change.

Flagged both in the Risk Management framework and separately by the Board, which noted the Company 'remains vigilant in addressing evolving cyber security threats to its IT systems', with Internal Audit monitoring control effectiveness across all locations.
A distribution business is directly exposed to disruption in the global technology supply chain feeding its inventory.
Named as a distinct risk the Risk Management Committee monitors, relevant given the Company's dependence on globally-sourced ICT components and hardware.
Demand volatility across the Company's General Trade, Modern Trade and E-Commerce customer base is explicitly tracked as a risk factor.
Competitive intensity in ICT distribution is monitored as a structural risk to market share and margins.
Changes in applicable regulation are tracked as a risk given the Company's compliance obligations across corporate, tax and listing regulations.

risks.risk: Working capital management and credit risk
risks.note: Distribution requires significant investment in inventory and receivables; the Risk Management Committee explicitly monitors working-capital management and credit risk as core operating risks.

one-line thesis: Rashi Peripherals delivered 43% YoY revenue growth in Q3FY26 driven by 50% volume and 50% ASP growth due to global component shortages and preponed corporate buying ahead of price hikes, with PAT up 132% — this reflects structural demand for AI-ready PCs in India, amplified by policy tailwinds, and positions the company to sustain revenue growth even with flattish unit volumes through pricing power and distribution scale.

Q3), +5% YoY (9M); EBITDA/margin: not disclosed; PAT (rptd): +132% YoY (Q3), +25% YoY (9M); PAT (normalized): adjusted for INR4cr gratuity/leave liability impact; order book: no large project orders in 9M FY26 (vs INR2,000cr in FY25); net debt: debt-equity 0.5x, blended borrowing cost 7.5-8% — one-off: INR4cr incremental liability from Labour Code 2025 recognition
guidance: revenue growth: sustained above 15-20% (base business), driven by ASP; margin: stable near 1.8-1.9% PAT margin; order inflow: no large project visibility; capex/commissioning: no new capex announced, branch expansion ongoing (55th in Solapur)
order book & pipeline: No large project orders in 9M FY26; growth entirely from base business (vs INR2,000cr project revenue in FY25)

growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into AI-ready solutions; UAE subsidiary for SAARC logistics; enterprise ecosystem build-out; deeper penetration into Tier 2/3 cities via 700+ distribution points

capex / expansion: No formal capex announced; organic branch expansion (55 branches, 55th in Solapur); focus on warehouse and service center network
capital allocation: Prioritizing reduction in borrowing cost (post-credit upgrade to AA-); maintaining debt-equity at ~0.5x; open to receivables discounting if it improves ROC/ROE; ESOP cost INR14cr YTD for talent retention
risks & watch-items: RAM/SSD price volatility; Micron consumer brand discontinuation (dent expected in FY27); affordability constraints reducing B2C demand; supply chain disruptions; potential debtor days increase if channel partners face liquidity stress

non-obvious takeaways: INR4cr Labour Code liability is a one-time accounting impact, not cash outflow; 50% volume growth in Q3 was unusually high due to preponed buying — sustainability hinges on continued price hikes; UAE subsidiary is for logistics, not revenue yet; no large project revenue in 9M FY26 means base business growth is even more impressive

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Rashi Peripherals (RP tech), established in 1989, is a value-added distributor of ICT products in India, sourcing from global technology brands and distributing through its Personal Computing, Enterprise & Cloud Solutions (PES) and Lifestyle & IT Essentials (LIT) business verticals. It serves General Trade (retailers, resellers, regional distributors), Modern Trade (large-format retailers) and E-Commerce customers, with growing participation in AI infrastructure, semiconductors, embedded electronics and digital learning.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- AI PC transition (NPU-equipped devices, Copilot+ PC platform, Windows 10 end-of-support) is driving a multi-year upgrade cycle and robust demand for GPUs, AI-enabled processors, memory modules, SSDs, cooling and power-management solutions.
- Enterprise refresh cycle: replacement of ageing devices and migration to AI-ready systems is accelerating commercial PC upgrades; India enterprise segment and workstation shipments grew strongly in Q1 2026.
- Data-centre build-out in India (installed capacity ~1.9 GW in FY26, more than doubling from ~778 MW in FY23, with a ~4.5 GW development pipeline over the next five years) is driving demand for servers, storage, networking, power-management and cooling infrastructure.
- Global and Indian semiconductor demand growth driven by AI-native infrastructure, hyperscale/cloud expansion, embedded/edge applications and supply-chain diversification is expected to increase distribution and technical-design-support opportunities.
- India's IT spending is projected to reach USD176.3 billion in 2026 (+10.6% YoY), with device spending forecast to rise 9.9% to USD66.4 billion, supported by enterprise modernisation, replacement demand and AI-enabled technology adoption.
- Gaming market growth (Indian gaming market projected to grow from USD4.59bn in FY25 to USD5.37bn in FY26, at a longer-term CAGR of 15.62%) driven by esports, cloud/multiplayer gaming and premiumisation of gaming devices/peripherals.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: As an asset-light ICT distributor (no manufacturing plants; BRSR discloses 0 plants and 70 domestic + 1 international office/branch locations), RP tech's 'expansion' is footprint and vertical build-out rather than physical capacity. During FY26 the Company added three new branches (Nanded, Baramati, Solapur), taking its branch network to 55 branches (71 warehouses, 700+ locations), deepening Tier-II/Tier-III presence. It strengthened its semiconductor and embedded vertical through its Bengaluru Embedded Lab (reference-design, board bring-up, PCB design and AI/ML application development) and by incorporating new semiconductor subsidiaries in India (Rashi Semiconductor Solutions Private Limited) and, after the FY26 close (post 1 April 2026), a Singapore step-down subsidiary (Rashi Semiconductor Solutions Pte Ltd, 100% held by the Indian semiconductor subsidiary) and a Dubai step-down subsidiary (Rashi Peripherals LLC-FZ, 98% held by Rashi Peripherals Pte Ltd, Singapore). It also incorporated a new wholly-owned subsidiary, RP Tech Electronics Limited. Subsequent to year-end, the Board (June 23, 2026) approved and completed (July 2, 2026) the acquisition of 67% of VDA Infosolutions Private Limited for Rs 368.50 crore cash, with the remaining 33% stake to be acquired over the next three years.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Diversified portfolio of 18,400+ SKUs spanning personal computing, enterprise infrastructure, components, storage, networking, lifestyle and emerging technology, enabling multi-segment participation across consumer, SMB and enterprise customers.
- Long-standing brand relationships: of 78 global technology brands represented, 23 brands associated for over 5 years contribute 88% of revenue, and 11 brands with relationships exceeding 10 years contribute 72% of revenue.
- One of India's largest ICT distribution ecosystems — 55 branches, 71 warehouses and presence across 700+ locations, serving 10,300+ partners and B2B customers across general trade, modern trade and e-commerce.
- Early mover in semiconductor distribution — first ICT distributor in India to enter the segment (2021) — supported by a dedicated Embedded Lab in Bengaluru.
